title: [AAFLOW+] Stateful Operator Abstraction with Zero-Copy Distributed KV Cache Orchestration for Multi-Agent Workflows
event_hint: AAFLOW+: distributed KV cache orchestration system for multi-agent LLM workflows
problem: Multi-agent LLM systems remain text-centric, requiring downstream agents to repeatedly recompute shared context through expensive prefill even when identical model state was already computed by upstream agents, causing increased TTFT, duplicated computation, and poor branch factor scalability for long-context workloads
mechanism: Stateful operator abstraction extending AAFLOW from dataflow to stateflow, treating KV cache as a first-class distributed systems object with operators for materialization, transfer, fork, restricted composition, and eviction; runtime uses zero-copy communication, Arrow-based formats, explicit metadata, and transfer-aware scheduling to enable efficient KV state transfer between distributed components

evidence.claim: Stateful execution reduces TTFT by up to 50.2× at long context (from abstract; baseline and conditions not visible in current evidence)
evidence.condition: long context; baseline conditions not visible in current evidence

evidence.claim: On HF backend with Mistral at long context, AAFLOW+ reaches 0.041s mean TTFT vs 2.057s for AAFLOW-text, 2.017s for dense prefill, and 0.704s for KVCOMM; DistServe style remains at 0.123s
evidence.condition: HF backend; Mistral model; long context

evidence.claim: Stateful execution achieves 7.60× speedup at 16-agent scale for Mistral (AAFLOW+ 224.39s vs SGLang prefix 1704.86s; dense prefill 2716.11s)
Stateful execution achieves 7.63× speedup at 16-agent scale for Llama3 (AAFLOW+ 220.05s vs SGLang prefix 1679.81s)
Reduces peak KV memory by 1.72–6.10× and improves throughput by more than 7.74× (from abstract; workload and hardware conditions not visible in current evidence)
evidence.condition: workload and hardware conditions not visible in current evidence

evaluation_context: GPU clusters; Mistral-7B and Llama-3-8B models; multi-agent workflows (planner-retriever-solver, tree-of-thought, collaborative RAG); HF, vLLM, and SGLang backends; comparison against text-based agent communication; analytical cost model parameterized by empirical hardware microbenchmarks; trace-driven model to isolate KV-transfer limits
limitations: Supplement provides partial experiment details (backends: HF, vLLM, SGLang; models: Mistral, Llama3) and specific TTFT/multi-agent latency comparisons, but key gaps remain: 50.2× TTFT, 1.72-6.10× memory, and 7.74× throughput claims lack visible baseline conditions and detailed configuration; specific network bandwidth thresholds for transfer vs recomputation decision not provided; network utilization, KVCache transmission volumes, and end-to-end P95 metrics not visible; synthetic deterministic prompts used with Y=64 output tokens; infrastructure assessments based on controlled experiments not production cluster data; scope focuses on shared-prefix multi-agent workflows not independent stateless inference; compatibility requires identical model architectures and positional encodings
project_relevance: Directly addresses TPN questions about state-aware scheduling reducing TTFT/TPOT and KVCache transmission overhead; KV transfer over moderate-to-high bandwidth networks vs recomputation decision criterion (Equation 7) is network-aware; zero-copy distributed KV cache orchestration provides network-side mechanisms beyond pure GPU memory scheduling; project asks whether network perceives KVCache location and Token performance targets—AAFLOW+ makes KV placement and transfer explicit in distributed execution graph

evidence_gaps.question: What are the specific network bandwidth thresholds and transfer costs where KV transfer outperforms recomputation (cited as moderate-to-high bandwidth)?
What are the exact network utilization, KVCache transmission volumes, and end-to-end P95 metrics for the multi-agent workflows?
